title: ABC News (@ABC) reports 15 to 20 Inches of Rain Flooding Roads in Brevard County, Florida
summary: ABC News (@ABC) reports that parts of Florida recorded 15 to 20 inches of rain, turning roads into rivers and submerging cars. The report centers on southeastern Brevard County, close to the single-day rainfall record for the state.
contents:
## Event

ABC News (@ABC) reports that between 15 and 20 inches of rain have fallen in parts of Florida, turning roads into rivers and submerging cars. The article describes the totals as close to the single-day rainfall record for the state. The current one-day record of 23.28 inches dates to 1980, when moisture from Hurricane Jeanne interacted with a stationary boundary over South Florida.

## Location and Time

ABC News (@ABC) places the observed totals in southeastern Brevard County in east central Florida. The article published at 22:06 UTC on November 2, 2026, which equals 5:06 PM Eastern Standard Time. The report notes that flash flood warnings remain in effect for West Melbourne, Palm Bay, and Grant-Valkaria, and that an additional 2 to 6 inches of rain remain possible. The map point marks the county as a bounded area, not a precise flood location.

## Evidence

The primary source comes from an ABC News article by Kenton Gewecke and Mary Kekatos. The article cites a Port St. Lucie Police Department video, a Brevard Public Schools Facebook notice that closed schools due to flooding on Monday, and a National Weather Service Melbourne warning that urges residents to move to higher ground. It also cites a National Weather Service Miami post on X. The queued ABC News post repeats the same rainfall range. No second independent outlet appears in the checked sources for the rainfall totals, so this event rests on attributed reporting from one publisher.

## Allied Relevance

United States emergency managers, transportation planners, and military installation staff can use documented flash-flood impacts on the Atlantic coast of Florida to judge road-network closures, school disruptions, and local infrastructure stress. Flooding that closes roads and strands vehicles in a populous coastal county provides situational awareness for civil response and logistics planning.

## Confidence and Gaps

Confidence in the rainfall range stays moderate because the totals come from a single publisher. The article does not describe the instruments or measurement period behind the 15 to 20 inch range. It reports no casualties, rescues with injuries, or property damage counts, and no official flood damage assessment appears in the checked sources. The claim that vehicles became submerged rests on the article lede and police comments about stranded vehicles.
